conflicts.description: Showcase-internal English-microcopy inconsistency, same root cause as mobile-home.json's conflicts[0]: the "MOBILE · 360" Explore frame's own bottom-nav row (line 1864) and the § 22 Explore frame's bottom-nav row (line 2109) both label item 3 "Learning", not "My Learning".

conflicts.description: ux/MOBILE_UX.md § 3 and product/INFORMATION_ARCHITECTURE.md § 3 both lock Learning Paths as living inside Explore via a "segment/tab" control. Neither of the two showcase Explore frames actually shows a segment/tab control anywhere — § 22's Explore frame instead shows a single brand-tinted LearningPathCard promo ("Become a Frontend Engineer", lines 2085-2089) inlined directly among the search/filter/course-card flow, with no visible tab strip switching between a "Courses" view and a "Learning Paths" view.
conflicts.resolution: Not resolved by this pass — genuinely ambiguous evidence, disclosed rather than guessed. Two readings are both plausible from the same 788px-tall captured frame: (a) the segment/tab control exists above the fold and simply isn't visible in this compact illustration, and the LearningPathCard shown is an unrelated in-feed promotional card that coexists with the tab control; or (b) the showcase's own composition deliberately promotes a single followed/recommended Learning Path inline rather than requiring a tab switch at all, and the rank-1 docs' 'segment/tab' language is the more literal source of truth to build against regardless. Rank-1 (product/UX) governs the BEHAVIOR (a segment/tab must exist, per SOURCE_MANIFEST.json precedence) — this spec's sections/componentSequence below include a segment/tab as required by rank-1, while also disclosing that the showcase's inline promo card is real visual evidence worth keeping alongside it, not a substitute for it.

rank-1-required segment/tab into Learning Paths (ux/MOBILE_UX.md § 3) — the showcase's own visible evidence is a single inline LearningPathCard promo instead (lines 2085-2089); see conflicts[1]
CourseCard list, 1 column full-width, full-width in-card CTA per the § 20 locked guidance quote (line 1918: "the card action goes full-width for thumb reach")
